correctness.rationale: In F_3^r, nilpotence of the augmentation ideal at exponent 2r+1 proves the Davenport bound. A 2r-term zero-sum-free sequence on distinct lines must have nonzero external subset return to every occupied line by the quotient F_3^{r−1} Davenport bound. The explicit six-vector rank-three seed has no zero-sum subset and occupies distinct lines; adjoining two final-coordinate-one vectors preserves those properties for all higher ranks. The rank-one/two converse follows by extremal length and a rank-two case analysis. Independent subset checks verified the seed and ranks 4,5, and exhausted rank-two zero-sum-free multisets of length at most 4. The result explicitly excludes empty subsums.
residual_risks: Only elementary ternary groups and nonempty subsequence sums; high-rank existence overlaps Gao–Geroldinger implications, while exact rank-three threshold is distinguished.
